findings.title: apt-get install without --no-install-recommends
findings.description: Installing recommended packages bloats the image with unneeded software, enlarging the attack surface. Pass --no-install-recommends to apt-get install.
findings.remediation: Review the flagged configuration against Docker and CIS Docker Benchmark best practices. Apply the control the rule describes, preferring restrictive defaults, least privilege, and audit logging. Validate with `aegis scan` after the change.

findings.title: apt-get update without cache cleanup
findings.description: apt-get update leaves package lists in the image layer. Remove /var/lib/apt/lists/* in the same RUN to keep layers lean.
findings.expected: clean package lists in the same RUN layer
findings.remediation: Review the flagged configuration against Docker and CIS Docker Benchmark best practices. Apply the control the rule describes, preferring restrictive defaults, least privilege, and audit logging. Validate with `aegis scan` after the change.

findings.title: sudo used in build
findings.description: RUN executes as root by default, so sudo is unnecessary; its presence suggests confused privilege boundaries or a copied snippet. Drop sudo and rely on USER instead.
findings.expected: run as root by default; use USER for runtime privilege drop
findings.remediation: Review the flagged configuration against Docker and CIS Docker Benchmark best practices. Apply the control the rule describes, preferring restrictive defaults, least privilege, and audit logging. Validate with `aegis scan` after the change.

findings.title: No WORKDIR directive
findings.description: Without WORKDIR the build and the container run from /, so relative paths and stray files land in the filesystem root. Set an explicit WORKDIR for the application.
findings.remediation: Review the flagged configuration against Docker and CIS Docker Benchmark best practices. Apply the control the rule describes, preferring restrictive defaults, least privilege, and audit logging. Validate with `aegis scan` after the change.

findings.title: No maintainer label
findings.description: Images without ownership metadata are harder to triage when a vulnerability is found. Add LABEL maintainer= or org.opencontainers.image.authors.
findings.remediation: Review the flagged configuration against Docker and CIS Docker Benchmark best practices. Apply the control the rule describes, preferring restrictive defaults, least privilege, and audit logging. Validate with `aegis scan` after the change.

findings.title: No STOPSIGNAL directive
findings.description: Without STOPSIGNAL the container gets SIGTERM, which apps that only handle SIGINT (or expect another signal) ignore until the orchestrator SIGKILLs them, risking data loss. Declare the signal your app handles for graceful shutdown.
findings.remediation: Review the flagged configuration against Docker and CIS Docker Benchmark best practices. Apply the control the rule describes, preferring restrictive defaults, least privilege, and audit logging. Validate with `aegis scan` after the change.

findings.title: Full OS base image
findings.description: Full Linux distributions carry hundreds of packages the app never uses, each a potential CVE. Prefer minimal bases (distroless, Chainguard, Alpine, or -slim variants).
findings.remediation: Review the flagged configuration against Docker and CIS Docker Benchmark best practices. Apply the control the rule describes, preferring restrictive defaults, least privilege, and audit logging. Validate with `aegis scan` after the change.

findings.title: apt-get install without pinned versions
findings.description: Unpinned apt packages float across rebuilds, making images non-reproducible and silently pulling new versions. Pin versions: apt-get install pkg=1.2.3.
findings.remediation: Review the flagged configuration against Docker and CIS Docker Benchmark best practices. Apply the control the rule describes, preferring restrictive defaults, least privilege, and audit logging. Validate with `aegis scan` after the change.

findings.title: Passwordless sudo configured (NOPASSWD)
findings.description: A RUN step writes a NOPASSWD entry to /etc/sudoers (or /etc/sudoers.d/), granting a user passwordless root. Any process running as that user — including a compromised application — can escalate to root without a password. Require a password for sudo, or drop sudo entirely and rely on USER for runtime privilege separation.
findings.evidence: RUN = NOPASSWD entry written to a sudoers file
findings.expected: no passwordless sudo entry in sudoers
findings.remediation: Remove the hardcoded secret immediately and rotate it. Use Docker secrets / Compose secrets or a secrets manager; never bake secrets into images or env files.
